activation: When analyst.json contains paper structure analysis or review analysis. Choose the narrative angle that creates the most tension. These are not mutually exclusive — combine as needed.

the_verdict_explained.summary: Why was this paper accepted or rejected? Lead with the decision, then unpack the evidence.
the_verdict_explained.core_tension: the gap between what the authors claim and what reviewers saw.

the_best_paper_autopsy.summary: What made this paper stand out? Lead with a specific, surprising quality (not 'it was good'). Use quantitative comparisons to other papers at the same venue.
the_best_paper_autopsy.best_for: award-winning papers, especially when the reasons aren't obvious.

the_reviewers_war.summary: When reviewers dramatically disagree. Lead with the most extreme divergence in opinion; show what each reviewer saw differently in the same paper.

the_missing_experiment.summary: What reviewers wanted but didn't get. Lead with what the paper could have shown but didn't; frame as a gap the reader can now understand.
the_missing_experiment.best_for: rejected papers where the core idea had merit.

the_method_behind_the_breakthrough.summary: Technical deep-dive made accessible. Lead with the real-world impact, then explain how it works; use analogies and progressive disclosure.
the_method_behind_the_breakthrough.best_for: genuinely novel methods a data-literate reader can appreciate.

before_and_after.summary: How this paper changed the field. Lead with what people believed before, contrast with after; show the citation trail as evidence of influence.
before_and_after.best_for: influential papers with clear downstream impact.

paper_specific_writing_rules: When discussing reviews, quote specific reviewer language — don't paraphrase into blandness.
Present both sides of reviewer disagreements before revealing the outcome.
Use paper figures directly when they tell the story better than words.
Frame technical contributions in terms of what they enable, not just what they are.
If the paper was rejected, maintain analytical respect — explain why the concerns mattered, don't mock.
